endorsements.quote: When a high-risk flag is triggered, the system initiates an alert to the designated nurse within a predefined time window (eg, immediate escalation for imminent risk and within 24 hours for high-risk but nonimminent flags), prompting nurse-led assessment and triage.
These realities are why we argue for a nurse-led, risk-tiered approach that matches oversight and evaluation to intended use and potential impact.
PCCPs should be updated using drift monitoring and postmarket findings.

A workable starting point is to define intended use and risk tier, assign a named human-in-the-loop lead with a clear escalation pathway, and track a small set of safety and outcome indicators; more complex elements such as federated evaluation infrastructure can be added later as staffing, governance capacity, and partnerships grow.
Data should be minimized and processed on the device when feasible, with auditable logs and role-based access.
Procurement can leverage established assessment criteria to mandate safety, interoperability, evidence thresholds, and transparency artifacts such as model cards and data sheets [ 17 , 23 , 24 ].
Red teaming and child safety audits should be refreshed annually.

unlisted_practices: Set limits on chatbot session length and frequency for youth so that engagement does not become a proxy for benefit.
Co-design youth-facing therapy chatbots with neurodiverse youth and caregivers and match language and reading level.
Implement content safety and age gating before deploying child-facing chatbots.
Obtain developmentally appropriate consent or assent and provide parental controls for minors using chatbots.
Distinguish HIPAA-governed health data from FERPA-governed education records and set appropriate data sharing agreements when care spans clinics and schools.
Document subgroup performance of AI chatbots and remediate disparities through targeted outreach, assistive technologies, and human review for edge cases.
Design chatbot tools for low-bandwidth or offline use and arrange device or connectivity support to promote equity.
Reimburse nurse-delivered triage, coaching, monitoring, and escalation work in chatbot-supported care.
Establish a federated real-world evidence and safety surveillance network using a shared harm taxonomy and standardized indicators.

Monitor a defined indicator set including access and equity, safety signals, time to escalation, model rollback events, clinical outcomes, user experience, supervision burden, and economic value, stratified by subgroup.
Integrate chatbots into measurement-based stepped care pathways with defined handoffs, tapering and exit criteria rather than parallel shadow care.
Convene a multistakeholder steering group including caregivers, students, regulators, payers and developers to agree risk tiers and intended use before deploying chatbots.
Run sandbox pilots and safety testing before scale-up and monitor postdeployment for drift and adverse events.
Require certification criteria and fairness audits for procured child-facing chatbots.

screen.reason: This is a Viewpoint paper proposing a nurse-led, risk-tiered policy and implementation framework for integrating AI therapy chatbots into pediatric ADHD care.
